name: TJA1043T_1J
title: High-speed CAN transceiver with standby, sleep and wake-up
summary: A high-speed CAN physical-layer transceiver for automotive networks, to ISO 11898-2:2003 and ISO 11898-5:2007, with loop-delay symmetry timing for CAN FD data phases up to 2 Mbit/s. It runs from a 5 V VCC, a battery supply VBAT for 12 V and 24 V systems and a separate VIO logic supply that matches 3 V and 5 V microcontrollers. Standby and Sleep modes with local (WAKE pin) and remote (bus) wake-up, an INH output to switch the node's regulators, a SPLIT output and a set of diagnostic flags read on ERR_N. Offered in SO14 and HVSON14, AEC-Q100 qualified.
key_figures: up to 2 Mbit/s (CAN FD data phase)
4.5 V to 40 V operating; 58 V load dump

circuits.title: Typical application with a 3 V microcontroller
circuits.description: A node that can switch off its own supplies. The battery comes in through a reverse-polarity diode and feeds a 5 V regulator for VCC, a 3 V regulator for VIO and the microcontroller, and VBAT through a series resistor. INH drives the enable inputs of both regulators, so in Sleep, where INH floats, the node's supplies are off while the transceiver stays powered from the battery. A switch to ground with a pull-up to the battery and a series resistor into WAKE gives a local wake-up. The microcontroller drives TXD, STB_N and EN and reads RXD and ERR_N. CANH and CANL carry a split termination of two resistors with a capacitor from the centre to ground, and SPLIT is tied to the centre.

circuits.title: Split termination on the SPLIT pin
circuits.description: The bus is terminated by two 60 Ω resistors in series between CANH and CANL; their centre goes to SPLIT and to a capacitor to ground. Inside, SPLIT is the middle of two equal resistors between VCC and GND that are switched in only in Normal and Listen-only modes, so it holds the centre at 0.5VCC there and floats in the other modes. This steadies the recessive bus level where other nodes leak current to ground, which lowers emission.
notes: Pins other than VCC, GND, CANH, CANL and SPLIT take no part in this circuit.

circuits.title: Test circuit for timing characteristics
circuits.description: The fixture for the dynamic characteristics. VCC and VIO share a +5 V supply decoupled by 47 µF and 100 nF, with EN and STB_N tied to it so the part sits in Normal mode. VBAT comes from +12 V through a diode with 10 µF to ground. A pulse generator drives TXD; the bus is loaded by RL in parallel with 100 pF, and RXD by 15 pF to ground. SPLIT, WAKE, ERR_N and INH are left open.
notes: RL is 60 Ω in the characteristics tables' conditions unless a row says otherwise.

operation.text: A stand-alone transceiver between a CAN protocol controller and the two-wire bus, for automotive high-speed CAN. It meets ISO 11898-2:2003 and ISO 11898-5:2007 and adds loop-delay symmetry figures so the CAN FD data phase can run at up to 2 Mbit/s. It is a third-generation part, following the TJA1041A with better EMC, ESD and quiescent current, and it is passive on the bus when unpowered. It suits 12 V and 24 V systems.

Three supplies: VCC (4.5 V to 5.5 V), the transceiver supply; VIO (2.8 V to 5.5 V), the supply of the I/O level adaptor; and VBAT (4.5 V to 40 V), the battery supply. VIO is tied to the microcontroller's supply so that the logic pins (EN, STB_N, TXD, RXD, ERR_N) work at its levels with no glue logic. With VBAT absent the part disengages from the bus (zero load).

Five modes, picked with STB_N and EN: Normal (STB_N HIGH, EN HIGH), Listen-only (STB_N HIGH, EN LOW), Standby, Go-to-Sleep and Sleep. STB_N LOW with EN LOW gives Standby; STB_N LOW with EN HIGH gives Go-to-Sleep, which turns into Sleep after th unless the Wake flag is set. Undervoltage flags override the pins as the mode selection table lists.
Driver and receiver both on. RXD gives the bus state, the bus edges are slope-controlled for low emission, the bus pins are biased to 0.5VCC through Ri and INH is on.
The transmitter is off; the receiver still reports the bus on RXD. The bus is still biased to 0.5VCC and INH stays on.

The first power-saving level. No transmit or receive; a low-power receiver watches the bus for a wake-up pattern. The bus pins are biased to ground through Ri and INH stays on. With VIO and VBAT present, RXD and ERR_N show a pending wake-up request.
Behaves as Standby while a sleep command is pending. After the hold time th (20 µs to 50 µs) the part enters Sleep, unless STB_N or EN changes or the Wake flag is set first.

The second power-saving level: as Standby, but INH floats, turning off the regulators it controls, and the VBAT current drops to its minimum. Sleep is reached through Go-to-Sleep, or directly when VCC or VIO stays under its undervoltage threshold longer than tdet(uv). A wake-up (local or remote) or the STB_N and EN pins bring the node back.

Set when VCC or VIO stays under its undervoltage threshold (Vuvd(VCC), Vuvd(VIO)) past tdet(uv). The part then goes to Sleep, so the bus is left alone and INH turns the regulators off, which also stops current into a shorted rail. A wake-up request, the Pwon flag or a rising edge on STB_N clears it and restarts the timers, as does VCC and VIO both recovering for longer than trec(uv); the mode then follows STB_N and EN.
Set when VBAT falls below Vuvd(VBAT). The part then tries for Standby and takes zero load from the bus. It clears when VBAT comes back, and the mode then follows STB_N and EN.

Set when VBAT comes back after falling below Vuvd(VBAT), which is normally a battery reconnection. It clears UVNOM and the timers and sets Wake and Wake-up source, so power-up behaves the same whatever the supply sequence. It is read on ERR_N in Listen-only mode and clears on entering Normal mode.

Set by a local or a remote wake-up request, in Standby, Go-to-Sleep or Sleep. Local: the WAKE level changes and stays at its new level for at least twake. Remote: a dominant phase of at least twake(busdom), a recessive phase of at least twake(busrec), then a second dominant phase of at least twake(busdom), the whole pattern inside tto(wake)bus. Setting Wake clears UVNOM and the timers; with VIO and VBAT present it shows at once on ERR_N and RXD. It is also set at power-on and clears when UVNOM is set or Normal mode is entered.

Set together with Wake when the wake-up came from the WAKE pin, so the controller can tell a local wake-up from a bus one. Read on ERR_N in Normal mode; set at power-on, cleared on leaving Normal mode.

Set when the part, driving the bus dominant, sees a short of a bus line to VBAT, VCC or GND over four dominant-recessive cycles in a row on TXD. Read on ERR_N in Normal mode; cleared at power-on or on entering Normal mode again.

Set in Normal and Listen-only modes by any of four local faults: TXD held dominant, TXD shorted to RXD, bus held dominant, or overtemperature. Read on ERR_N in Listen-only mode. It clears at power-on, on entering Normal mode, or when RXD is dominant while TXD is recessive once all the faults have gone.

If TXD stays LOW longer than tto(dom)TXD (0.3 ms to 1.5 ms) the transmitter is switched off, so a stuck controller cannot hold the whole bus dominant. The time-out sets the lowest usable bit rate, 40 kbit/s. The transmitter stays off until the Local failure flag is cleared.

A short between TXD and RXD would latch the bus dominant once driven, since the RXD low-side driver normally overpowers the controller's high-side TXD drive. The part detects this and switches the transmitter off until the Local failure flag is cleared.

A bus short or a faulty node can hold the differential voltage in the dominant range, which the normal bus failure check misses because no node starts sending on a dominant bus. If the bus stays dominant longer than tto(dom)bus the Local failure flag is set, and the transmitter is left on. This flag is not latched for this fault: it drops as soon as the bus goes recessive.
An excessive junction temperature switches the transmitter off to protect the output drivers; Tj(sd) is 190 °C typ. The transmitter stays off until the Local failure flag is cleared.

Used with a split termination it steadies the recessive bus level and lowers emission in networks where unpowered nodes leak to ground. In Normal and Listen-only modes it outputs 0.5VCC; in Standby, Go-to-Sleep and Sleep it floats.

Either edge on WAKE is a local wake-up event. After twake the internal bias follows the pin's state to save current: a pull-up to VBAT when the pin is HIGH, a pull-down to GND when it is LOW. Where local wake-up is not used, WAKE should be tied to VBAT or GND for best EMI performance.
INH is HIGH (within ΔVH of VBAT) in every mode but Sleep, where it floats, so regulators enabled from it switch the node's supplies off in Sleep.
On HVSON14 the exposed centre pad is soldered to board ground for thermal and electrical performance.
AEC-Q100 Rev-G qualified for automotive use. Halogen free and RoHS compliant. The HVSON14 package is leadless, 3.0 mm × 4.5 mm, and its joints are easier to check by automated optical inspection.

All pins have ESD protection for normal handling; handle per JESD625-A or an equivalent. Reflow peak temperatures follow J-STD-020D by package thickness and volume. Smaller packages run hotter in reflow. Observe the moisture sensitivity precautions marked on the packing.
